source: Real CT images from TCIA collections (see sources); tools/make_real_ct.py

real-ct-noise.label: Four real CT scans of a uniform block of a test phantom at tube currents of 50, 100, 200, and 400 mA, each with its measured noise
real-ct-noise.cap: Real scans of a uniform plastic block in a test phantom, on one scanner (GE Discovery STE, 120 kVp, 1.25 mm slices, standard kernel). Only the tube current changes. Each tile is a 34 mm square at a window of ±40 HU around the block's mean. Phantom data: TCIA CC-Radiomics-Phantom-2 (CC BY 3.0).

views.label: Tube current
views.facts: Noise is the standard deviation of the HU in a 51 mm square of the block (mean 121 HU): 13.5, 9.5, 6.7, and 4.7 HU at 50, 100, 200, and 400 mA. Noise ∝ 1 / √(tube current) predicts 13.5, 9.5, 6.7, and 4.8 HU from the 50 mA value: the measurements agree within 1%.

real-ct-kernel.label: A real textured block of a test phantom reconstructed with a soft, a standard, a lung, and an edge kernel from the same scan
real-ct-kernel.cap: One scan of a textured block in a test phantom (GE Discovery STE, 120 kVp, 65 mA, 1.25 mm slices), reconstructed with four kernels. Each tile is a 47 mm square. The noise under each tile is the standard deviation of the HU in a uniform block scanned at the same time and reconstructed with the same kernel. Phantom data: TCIA CC-Radiomics-Phantom-2 (CC BY 3.0).

views.label: Kernel
views.facts: Same raw data, four kernels: the noise in the uniform block is 10, 13, 54, and 91 HU. The soft kernel smooths the texture and the noise, and the edge kernel keeps the finest detail and the most noise.

real-ct-cbct.label: A real planning CT and cone-beam CT of the same patient at the same level, in the upper abdomen and the lower chest
real-ct-cbct.cap: Real images of one patient treated for pancreatic cancer: the planning CT (Philips Brilliance Big Bore, iterative reconstruction) and a cone-beam CT from the linac (Varian, reconstructed with the Ram-Lak filter), which the dataset's authors aligned to the planning CT. Both are shown at the same window. Data: TCIA Pancreatic-CT-CBCT-SEG (CC BY 4.0).
real-ct-cbct.head: Level

views.label: Upper abdomen
views.facts: Noise in the liver (SD of a 23 mm square): 12 HU on the planning CT and 20 HU on the cone-beam CT. The same square reads 115 HU on the planning CT, where the vessels are enhanced, and 44 HU on the cone-beam CT, where they are not.

views.label: Lower chest
views.facts: At this level the cone-beam field of view cuts off the patient's right side (the left of the image): anatomy outside the reconstruction diameter is missing.

real-ct-metal.label: A real chest CT with metal implants, reconstructed from the same data without and with iterative metal artifact reduction, at the level of the spine and the shoulders
real-ct-metal.cap: One real chest CT (Siemens SOMATOM go.Top, 100 kVp, 3 mm slices) with metal implants, reconstructed from the same raw data in two ways: the standard reconstruction (left) and Siemens iMAR, an iterative metal artifact reduction (right). Both are shown at the window 40 ± 200 HU. Data: TCIA CMB-LCA (CC BY 4.0).
real-ct-metal.head: Level
